title: DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme (Master's Scholarships for Public Policy and Good Governance)
overview: DAAD scholarships for master's degrees in public policy, governance and development at seven German courses, for graduates from developing and emerging countries who have a strong first degree and relevant practical experience. The application period for the 2027 intake (1 June to 31 July 2026) is over.
city: Passau, Duisburg-Essen, Erfurt and other participating universities
program_dates: Master's studies start in September or October of the intake year
deadline_text: Official call (Stipendienausschreibung 05/2026, study from September/October 2027): 'The application period for all seven higher education institutions is from 1 June until 31 July 2026.' Selection October/November 2026; applicants informed December 2026/January 2027. The programme page and database entry give no dates and defer to this announcement.
expected_next_cycle: No call for the 2028 intake is published. The 2027 call ran 1 June to 31 July 2026; if the yearly pattern holds the next period would again fall in June and July 2027, but no page states it.
funding_details: Official call (Stipendienausschreibung 05/2026, for studies from September/October 2027): scholarship 'of currently EUR 992 per month'; health insurance cover in Germany; 'fixed travel allowances (lump sums)' between Germany and the home country; a study and research grant; rent subsidies and family supplements 'as applicable'
'DAAD scholarship holders are exempt from paying tuition fees'
A preceding German language course in Germany of up to 4 months is mandatory (the programme page says up to six months)
The call does not use the words 'fully funded'; 'Social Protection' pays EUR 500 a month in its online fourth semester
participation_fee: No application fee is mentioned in the call
stipend: EUR 992 a month (current rate in the call), plus a study and research grant, rent subsidies and family supplements as applicable
eligibility: Graduates from developing and emerging countries (bachelor or equivalent) with a well-qualified first university degree and above-average grades (upper third) in Social and Political Sciences, Law, Economics, Public Policy and Administration
Willing to actively contribute to the social, political and economic development of their home country or region
Practical experience relevant to the programme (professional experience, internships, political or social commitment); the minimum depends on the master's course
Last university degree not older than six years at the time of application (not issued before 1 January 2020)
Candidates who already hold a master's degree must argue why they should be funded for another one
Not more than 15 months in the past spent in a country not on the DAC list
nationality_requirements: Graduates from developing and emerging countries; the Democratic Republic of the Congo (L) is on the DAC list of ODA recipients attached to the call and 'Congo, Democratic Republic' is on the DAAD database country list
Candidates who spent more than the past 15 months in a country not on the DAC list are not eligible
education_requirement: First university degree (bachelor or equivalent) with above-average grades (upper third) in Social and Political Sciences, Law, Economics, Public Policy and Administration; last degree not more than six years old (issued on or after 1 January 2020). Each course adds its own rules (for example Social Protection names Economics/Business Administration degrees and a written entry exam; the Passau courses need 60 ECTS in social sciences or economics and 10 ECTS of research methods)
experience_requirement: Practical experience relevant to the programme is required: 'professional experience, internships, political/social commitment'. Minimums by course: Magdeburg 3 months (or study abroad), Passau 4 months, Social Protection 5 months, Duisburg-Essen one year full-time, Erfurt one year, Osnabruck two years in the non-profit sector
language_requirement: Proof of English required, level set by each course (Magdeburg C1, Osnabruck B2; others 'very good' or 'excellent')
documents_required: One letter of motivation (maximum two pages)
Europass CV with date of issue
Full transcript with an explanation of the grading system
Confirmations of relevant professional experience, internships or community service on headed paper
A written reference from the current employer or a university lecturer, only if currently employed or a student
application_process: Apply directly to up to two of the seven participating master's courses (not to the DAAD) during the application period, with the same letter of motivation for both
A DAAD selection committee meets in October or November 2026; proposed candidates are asked by the DAAD to upload full documents; all applicants hear in December 2026 or January 2027
2027 call: the application period for all seven institutions ran from 1 June until 31 July 2026

sources.label: DAAD current announcement, Helmut-Schmidt-Programme 2027 (PDF, 05/2026): eligibility, funding, application period
DAAD: information about the master's courses (PDF): course prerequisites
DAAD: DAC list of ODA recipients (PDF attached to the call; the DRC is listed as an LDC)

eligibility_reason: The DRC is on the DAC list, the 2024 degree is inside the six-year limit and the internships count as practical experience. The call asks for above-average grades (upper third) and a degree in social or political sciences, law, economics, public policy or administration; the profile records neither the grade nor how Business Administration is classified, and each course sets its own English and experience rules.
potential_issues: The application period for the 2027 intake (1 June to 31 July 2026) is over; no 2028 call is published
Above-average grades (upper third) are required; the degree grade is not recorded

Course prerequisites differ: a written entry exam (Social Protection), 60 ECTS in social sciences or economics and 10 ECTS in research methods (Passau), one to two years of experience (Duisburg-Essen, Erfurt, Osnabruck)
A mandatory German course of up to four months in Germany precedes the degree
Applications go to the master's courses, not to the DAAD, and applications sent to more than two institutions are excluded
An earlier version of this record said no experience was required; the call asks for relevant practical experience and sets minimums by course
benefits: Master's in public policy or governance in Germany, with tuition waived
Monthly scholarship, health insurance and travel lump sums
German language course before the degree
Events, seminars and networking for scholarship holders
relevance_reason: The subject area matches the interests in public-sector and policy analysis and programme coordination, and the internships can count as the practical experience the call asks for. The upper-third grade rule and each course's prerequisites are not confirmed, and the window is closed until the next call.
upfront_cost_risk: Low: no application fee is mentioned
action: Nothing is open. Use the winter to check your Licence grade against the 'upper third' rule and the transcript against the course prerequisites (Social Protection at Bonn-Rhein-Sieg names Business Administration degrees and asks for five months of related experience), book an English test, and watch daad.de for the next call (the 2027 call ran 1 June to 31 July 2026).
notes: On 12 October 2026 the programme page and database entry gave no dates; both defer to the 'Current Announcement'. WebFetch got HTTP 503 on the programme page; it was read with a direct request. 2 November 2026 (rerun): the call PDF was read in full on static.daad.de (earlier cycles had only the programme page and a secondary summary). The 1 June to 31 July 2026 application period is now official, and the old 'no experience required' reading was wrong: the call requires relevant practical experience, internships included.

title: ICANN Fellowship Program
organization: ICANN (Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers)
overview: Fellows receive training, a mentor and travel assistance to attend an ICANN Public Meeting. The round opening in November 2026 is reserved for past fellows; the next round for first-time applicants has not been announced.
program_dates: ICANN meetings: 13-18 March 2027 (Community Forum) and 14-17 June 2027 (Policy Forum)
deadline_text: The round for the ICANN88 Community Forum is closed. The round for the ICANN89 Policy Forum opens 5 November 2026 and closes 5 December 2026, but only Fellowship alumni may apply for a Policy Forum fellowship.
funding_details: 'Travel assistance to attend the meeting is also provided.' Components are not itemised on the page read.
eligibility: At least 21 years of age when applying
Interested in, or already engaged in, ICANN's work on policy, the Domain Name System and Internet security and stability
Not involved in another ICANN-supported travel programme at the time of selection
nationality_requirements: No nationality restriction stated on the page read
application_process: Apply online during the round for a given ICANN meeting
eligibility_reason: The conditions are being at least 21 and being 'interested in, or already engaged in' ICANN's work on policy, the Domain Name System and Internet security. The profile's interests (operations, business analysis, programme coordination, public-sector research) do not record any interest in or engagement with Internet governance, so that criterion is unconfirmed.
potential_issues: No round currently open to first-time applicants
Needs a demonstrated interest in domain names and Internet policy
benefits: Travel to an ICANN Public Meeting
relevance_reason: A travel-funded route few people consider, though it is a stretch for a business profile without Internet-governance activity.
action: Low priority. Pair it with the Internet Society training if that field interests you.
notes: 2 November 2026 (rerun): fellowship page re-read; the ICANN88 round is closed, the ICANN89 Policy Forum round (5 November to 5 December 2026) is for Fellowship alumni only. Label lowered from LIKELY to POSSIBLY ELIGIBLE because interest in ICANN's work is not recorded in the profile.

title: Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders 2027
organization: U.S. Department of State (administered by IREX)
overview: Six-week executive-style Leadership Institute at a U.S. college or university in summer 2027 for about 550 young African leaders. Applications are open until 13 October 2026 and there is no application fee.
program_dates: Fellowship begins in the United States in June 2027 (six-week institute)
deadline_text: Last cycle closed on 2026-10-13. Next cycle not announced yet.
expected_next_cycle: Applications for the 2027 Fellowship closed on 13 October 2026. No 2028 call is announced on the official site (read 26 October 2026).
funding_details: 'If you are selected for the Fellowship, the U.S. Government will cover all program costs' (2027 application instructions)

Listed costs: J-1 visa support; round-trip travel from the Fellow's home city to the United States and domestic U.S. travel as required by the program; a six-week institute; a limited accident and sickness benefit plan; housing and meals during the program; an optional four-week Professional Development Experience (for up to 50 Fellows)
Not covered: salaries while away from work and personal purchases
'There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship.'
participation_fee: None: 'There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship.'
eligibility: Between the ages of 25 and 35 on or before the application deadline, 'although exceptional applicants ages 21-24 may be considered'
Citizen of an eligible country; the list includes the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
Resident of an eligible Sub-Saharan African country, permanently residing there as of 1 February 2027 and in June 2027
Not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident; eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa
Proficient in reading, writing and speaking English
Selection criteria include a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security, and a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa
nationality_requirements: Democratic Republic of the Congo is on the list of eligible countries
age_requirement: 25 to 35 at the deadline; exceptional applicants aged 21 to 24 may be considered
documents_required: Semi-finalists: international passport if available, or other government-issued photo ID, at the Embassy interview
application_process: October 2026 to January 2027: semi-finalists interviewed by U.S. embassies and consulates
February/March 2027: applicants notified of their status
March to May 2027: visa processing and pre-Fellowship activities for finalists
June 2027: Fellowship begins in the United States

sources.label: About the Fellowship ('Applications for the 2027 Mandela Washington Fellowship are now closed.')
2027 application instructions (PDF: deadline, eligibility incl. DRC, financial provisions, timeline)

eligibility_reason: DRC citizens living in the DRC can apply and English is at professional level. The age rule is 25 to 35, with only exceptional applicants of 21 to 24 considered, and the profile records only an under-30 band. Selection turns on a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, technology, governance or security, which the profile does not record.
potential_issues: The track record expected (business, trade, technology, governance or security) is thin on the recorded profile
Nationals of countries under a full or partial U.S. entry or visa suspension can apply, but finalists are selected case by case: check travel.state.gov for the DRC's current status
Finalists need a passport valid through at least 28 February 2028; passport status is not recorded
'J-1 visa support' and a 'limited accident and sickness benefit plan' are the stated visa and insurance terms; no salary replacement
benefits: Six-week institute at a U.S. university
Network of African and American leaders
Possible six-week Professional Development Experience afterwards
relevance_reason: The business and governance focus matches the degree and the Ministry internship. The weak point is the leadership record, which the application essays would have to carry.

visa.support: J-1 visa; processing takes place March to May 2027 for finalists.

action: Applications for 2027 are closed. If you applied, semi-finalist interviews at the U.S. Embassy run until January 2027 and notifications come in February/March 2027; otherwise watch mandelawashingtonfellowship.org for the 2028 call.
notes: 26 October 2026: /apply/, /apply-faqs/ and /2027-application-instructions/ now return HTTP 404 (taken down after the deadline). The About page states that 2027 applications are closed; the instructions PDF is still online and unchanged (deadline, eligibility, DRC on the country list, 'the U.S. Government will cover all program costs', no application fee). The application portal apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org still loads a login page. The '2027 Reciprocal Exchange Component' news item (deadline November 11, 2026) is for U.S. professionals, not African applicants. [auto 2026-10-28] Cycle closed. The details below describe the previous cycle and must be re-verified when the next call opens. 2 November 2026 (rerun): label lowered from LIKELY to POSSIBLY ELIGIBLE because the exact age and a record of accomplishment are not in the profile. The 2027 cycle is closed.

title: Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship (2027/2028)
overview: Hungarian government scholarship for bachelor's, master's and doctoral study in Hungary, offered through partner countries. The DRC is listed as a sending partner. The 2027/2028 call was not yet published on 2 October 2026.
program_dates: 2027/2028 academic year for the next call
deadline_text: No 2027/2028 call seen on 19 or 29 October 2026. The apply page still shows the 'Call for Applications 2026/2027' with the deadline '15th January 2026, 2 pm (CET)', and the latest news items (to 29 September 2026) do not announce a new call.
expected_next_cycle: The previous call opened on 17 November 2025 and closed on 15 January 2026 (2 pm CET). If the pattern holds, the next call could open in mid-November 2026 with a mid-January 2027 deadline. Not announced as of 29 October 2026.
funding_details: Monthly stipend at bachelor's and master's level: HUF 43,700 (about EUR 110)
Free dormitory place, or HUF 40,000 per month (about EUR 100) toward accommodation
Health care under Hungarian legislation plus supplementary medical insurance up to HUF 65,000 per year
stipend: HUF 43,700 per month (about EUR 110) at master's level
eligibility: Citizens of sending partners; 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' appears on the official partner list
nationality_requirements: Democratic Republic of the Congo is listed as a sending partner
application_process: Apply online in the Stipendium Hungaricum system during the call
Check how the DRC sending partner nominates candidates
eligibility_reason: The DRC is on the official list of sending partners and the profile holds the bachelor's degree needed for a master's application. The Apply page's FAQ says 'only the nominated applicants can proceed with their applications'; the DRC authority's nomination step and the study fields agreed for the DRC are not recorded, so eligibility is unconfirmed.
potential_issues: The stipend is about EUR 110 per month, so living costs need other funds
Travel is not mentioned as covered
Nomination by the DRC sending partner: procedure not verified
relevance_reason: Accessible on paper for a DRC bachelor's graduate, but the small stipend means it is only workable with savings or family support.
upfront_cost_risk: Flight and first months of living costs are likely to be self-funded.
action: Look at the official site from November 2026 for the 2027/2028 call, and find out which DRC authority handles nominations.
notes: 2 November 2026: the Apply page still shows only the 2026/2027 round (deadline 15 January 2026, 2 pm CET) and says there is one application deadline each year. No 2027/2028 call yet; the previous call opened on 17 November 2025. 2 November 2026 (rerun, Apply page re-read): FAQ confirms nomination by the sending country is required and that the online application and admission exams are free of charge; no 2027/2028 call yet. Label lowered from LIKELY to POSSIBLY ELIGIBLE.

title: Nasser Fellowship for International Leadership
organization: Egyptian Ministry of Youth and Sports (Nasser Youth Movement)
overview: Leadership fellowship held in Egypt for young leaders from all countries. The 2026 batch has closed its submissions and the next batch has not been announced.
deadline_text: Next batch not announced on 12 October 2026. The home page's news (latest items dated October 2026) concerns alumni; no application form for a new batch is shown.
expected_next_cycle: Next batch expected in 2027 if the yearly pattern holds; the 2026 batch closed its submissions by late March 2026.
funding_details: The criteria page read does not state which costs are covered.
eligibility: Aged between 18 and 40
Open to youth from all countries worldwide
Proficiency in English, the official language of the fellowship
Targets decision-makers, civil society activists, youth council leaders and similar profiles; international experience is one of the evaluation criteria
application_process: Application form published on the Nasser Youth Movement site when a batch opens
eligibility_reason: The general conditions are met: age 18 to 40, open to all countries, English, not resident in Egypt. The selection criteria list eligible profiles (decision-makers, alumni of AU and UN programmes, civil society activists, heads of youth councils) and favour applicants with a community project and international experience; the profile records none of these.
potential_issues: Selection favours established youth leaders: the criteria page lists decision-makers, programme alumni, civil society activists and heads of youth councils, and scores international experience and a social-impact project
relevance_reason: A travel opportunity with broad eligibility that standard scholarship searches miss.
action: Look at the site again in January 2027 for the next batch.
notes: 2 November 2026 (rerun): criteria page (dated 1 March 2025) re-read; general conditions unchanged. Label lowered from LIKELY to POSSIBLY ELIGIBLE.
